blocks.text: Scope the case to the composer and current turn: composition-safe text input with transient IME state, autosizing, attachment readiness, account-scoped draft persistence, one idempotent send command, streamed assistant state, idempotent Stop, retry, and focus recovery. Older history is an abstract paged input, not a database-design exercise.

What you are solving:
A composer where text input survives IME composition, attachments expose readiness, the sent turn appears immediately, and one correlated assistant response streams without stale chunks changing a newer turn.

Decision surface:
- Composition and keyboard semantics across desktop and mobile.
- Draft, attachment, pending-send, and stream state ownership.
- Idempotent send and correlated sequence handling.
- Stop versus transport abort and authoritative terminal status.
- Draft loss, attachment failure, uncertain send, and focus recovery.

steps.title: 1. Restore composer
steps.text: Load the current conversation shell, recent messages, and a scoped local draft without blocking the input.

steps.title: 2. User submits prompt
steps.text: After composition ends and required attachments are ready, snapshot text under a client message ID, create a pending command, and clear only the active draft revision.

steps.title: 3. Stream assistant reply
steps.text: Create an assistant placeholder and append chunks as they arrive. Show a streaming indicator and a Stop button.

steps.title: 4. End or cancel
steps.text: On completion, mark the assistant message phase as complete. If the user stops, keep partial text and reconcile the stopped terminal phase.

steps.title: 5. Reconcile current turn
steps.text: Merge the echoed user message and authoritative assistant terminal state by command, message, and stream identity.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: Is this a single conversation or many conversations per user?
Is the draft scoped to conversation, account, tab, or device?
Do we need real-time streaming or is a full response acceptable?
What is the max prompt/response size the UI should handle?
Which attachment phases block send, and which can be removed independently?
Should the user be able to stop/cancel generation?

blocks.title: Composer reliability and accessibility expectations
items: Latency should feel low with streaming chunks.
UI remains responsive even with long conversations.
Stale responses should not overwrite newer ones.
Data is stored safely and can be retrieved reliably.
Errors show a clear retry state without losing the prompt.

blocks.title: Composer and turn state boundaries
rows: Unsent text never becomes a conversation message, and mounted-control IME state is never persisted
Send references only finalized attachment IDs
Late acknowledgements and deltas cannot cross command identity

items.label: Primary transport
items.helperText: Keeps the UI responsive during long replies.

items.label: Key UX controls
items.helperText: Users can cancel or recover on failure.

blocks.title: Scope checkpoint
blocks.text: The design is coherent when composition-safe input, recoverable local intent, one send identity, sequenced stream updates, and honest Stop or retry behavior use the same turn model.

The browser owns composition-safe input, autosizing, attachment state, draft persistence, send commands, stream presentation, cancellation, and focus recovery. Server-side model execution and durable conversation history stay behind abstract current-turn and paged-history contracts; this design stops at composer, message, and stream behavior.
